title: radio.py/metrics.py: evolving collision frozenset inflates collision_rate
description:
## Problem

`Metrics.record_collision` is idempotent per `(rx_node_id, frozenset(tx_ids))` (`python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py`). That only dedups a stable overlapping set. `radio.py` `_get_rx_result_internal` re-resolves the current candidate list on every poll and, when `resolve_reception` returns None with >=2 candidates, calls `record_collision(node_id, tx_ids)` with whatever is audible now.

The 1 ms poll loop (metrics.py docstring) and HIL `deliver_pending_packets` therefore observe an evolving set as multiple collision identities:

1. **Set grows.** Poll sees {A,B} -> 1 collision. TX C starts. Next poll sees {A,B,C} -> 2nd collision.
2. **Set shrinks.** {A,B,C} counted; A ends; {B,C} is a new key -> 3rd collision. Then B ends and C is delivered -> `record_reception` as well.
3. **Success then collision.** Polling `get_rx_result` does not leave RX (9098.21 still returns the payload). First poll with only A records a reception. B starts. Next poll records a collision for {A,B}. Same receiver, same airtime, both `receptions` and `collisions` increment. Callback `deliver_pending_packets` cannot do this (it exits RX_WAIT on first success).

`test_collision_counted_once` starts both TXs then polls a stable pair; `test_collision_dedup` documents different frozensets as new events. Neither covers a set that changes while the node is still being polled. `record_collision` from radio.py also omits `channel` and `time_us`, so `collisions_by_channel` and collision rows in `_time_series` stay empty on the live path while the scalar `collisions` counter inflates.

This is not 9098.21 (repeat polls of the same delivery/notify). It is not 9098.15 (stash TTL / ghost collide). The identity key is working as specified for a frozen set; the poller feeds it a new set every time a TX starts or ends.

## Why this is security (metric inflation)

`collision_rate` is `collisions / (collisions + receptions)` and is exported to the dashboard, CSV, and `compare_metrics` A/B verdicts. Counting every frozenset snapshot -- and counting a decode plus a later overlap as both a delivery and a collision -- inflates the rate as a function of poll cadence and staggered TX starts. Capacity and CSMA studies then report more collisions than the receiver actually experienced as distinct events.

## Files

- `python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py` (`_get_rx_result_internal` collision arm; no channel/time_us)
- `python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py` (`record_collision` key = instantaneous frozenset)
- `python/tests/sim/test_metrics.py` (`test_collision_counted_once` stable pair only)
design: Key collisions by a continuous overlap interval at a receiver (for example (rx_node_id, collision_epoch) that stays open while candidate count >= 2 and closes when it drops to 0/1), not by each distinct frozenset snapshot. A reception already recorded for (rx, tx_id) must not also emit a later collision that includes that tx_id unless that is an explicit capture-then-interfere model with a test. Pass channel and time_us from radio.py so collisions_by_channel and CSV time-series match the scalar counter. Callback path unchanged (still one observe). Add a test: start TX A, poll (reception), start TX B overlapping, poll again -- collisions must not increment if A was already delivered to that rx; start A and B together, then C while overlapping, poll throughout -- collisions == 1 for that receiver until the overlap ends.
acceptance_criteria: Staggered overlapping TXs polled every 1 ms at one receiver count one collision for the overlap, not one per frozenset change. get_rx_result success then a later overlapping TX does not increment both receptions and collisions for the same (rx, first tx). Two TXs started together still count collisions==1 on repeated polls (existing test). radio.py record_collision populates collisions_by_channel and a time-series collision row. deliver_pending_packets still records at most one collision notify.
close_reason: Radio collision epoch stays open while candidates>=2; evolving frozensets do not inflate collisions. Already-delivered tx_ids do not also count as a collision. Channel/time_us passed through.
